vision noun

something seen in a dream or a trance

also apparition, a vision, see a vision

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.97: vīsa somniōrum (Lewis & Short)
Prop. 2.26.20; Ov. Am. 3.5.32

vīsum, vīsī n.

noun, second declension

something seen, a vision

Anything seen, and so a sight in sleep. In Cicero’s philosophy it also renders Greek φαντασία, an impression on the senses (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • speciēs, speciēī f. — an appearance in sleep, an apparition

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 8.6: in quiēte utrīque cōnsulī eadem dīcitur vīsa speciēs virī (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Ov.; also Liv.)

    First a sight, an outward look or appearance, then a figure seen in sleep; its everyday senses are look, appearance, beauty, pretext, and kind (Lewis & Short).

  • vīsiō, vīsiōnis f. — an apparition, a vision

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.120 (Lewis & Short)

    In Cicero chiefly an idea or image in the mind; a vision or apparition in the Fathers and Gregory, and the word of church Latin for the visions of the prophets and saints.

  • vīsus, vīsūs m. — a thing seen, an apparition

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 8.6.11: nocturnī vīsūs (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 3.36

    Its first sense is sight (see vision, sight).

Examples

  • in quiēte utrīque cōnsulī eadem dīcitur vīsa speciēs virī

    in their sleep, they say, the same figure of a man appeared to both consulsLiv. 8.6 (Lewis & Short)

See also dream, nightmare, vision.
